title: Learning in Agentic Systems
subtitle: Choose between learning through context and changing model parameters
summary: Pip’s guide repeats a failed route. The team can improve context with reviewed examples and reflections, or invest in changing model weights. Pip tests whether each lesson generalizes: remembering one success is not the same as improving the next visitor’s experience.

concepts.title: Nonparametric learning
concepts.body: Pip saves a reviewed example of an ambiguous ticket cancellation. Nonparametric learning changes behavior through examples, reflections, or retrieved experience without updating weights. The guidance is easy to revise but consumes context. Pip tests unfamiliar cases so remembered successes do not become overfitting.

concepts.title: Exemplar learning
concepts.body: Pip replaces twenty irrelevant greetings with three reviewed partial-refund examples. Exemplars guide behavior through patterns in the prompt. Quality and context limits constrain how much more examples help. Pip evaluates amount and currency selection rather than counting demonstrations.

concepts.title: Reflexion
concepts.body: Pip’s guide requests shipment details before identifying the order. Reflexion logs the trial, critiques the failure, updates memory, and injects the reflection into a later attempt. Pip checks whether the sequence actually improves. The extra loop adds latency and can preserve a mistaken critique.

concepts.title: Fine-tuning
concepts.body: Pip trains on reviewed structured tool calls. Fine-tuning updates model weights and can make behavior more consistent. Training costs, data quality, regressions, and evaluation burden may outweigh the benefit. Pip checks held-out requests before promoting the model, not just the examples it learned.

misconceptions.claim: Nonparametric learning is provided automatically by a more capable model.
misconceptions.correction: Nonparametric techniques improve behavior without changing model weights, for example by adding examples, reflections, or retrieved experience. They are easier to revise but consume context and can overfit to remembered cases.

misconceptions.claim: Exemplar learning removes the need for evaluation or human judgment.
misconceptions.correction: Providing successful examples in a prompt guides behavior through pattern matching. More examples can help, but context limits and example quality constrain the benefit. Evaluation and appropriate oversight remain necessary.

scenario.title: Learning from failed deliveries
scenario.context: A delivery agent repeatedly chooses an unavailable route. The team has few labeled examples.

options.label: Add reviewed reflections to memory and test them on new routes
options.benefit: Improves behavior without immediate weight training.
options.cost: Memory and review add latency and can encode a bad critique.
options.consequence: A held-out route improves while the original failure remains auditable.

options.label: Fine-tune immediately
options.benefit: May make a broad behavior change.
options.cost: Training data and regression checks are not ready.
options.consequence: The model improves one route class while regressing another.

scenario.debrief: Both choices can fit different constraints. The decision should state stakes, reversibility, evidence, and who owns correction.

quiz.question: An agent retrieves examples from prior tasks without changing model weights. What kind of improvement is this?
options: A change to the model architecture.
quiz.explanation: External examples can influence behavior at inference time without updating the model’s parameters.

quiz.question: What does Reflexion add after a failed attempt?
options: A guarantee that the next attempt will succeed.
A rule to repeat the same tool call indefinitely.
A reflection stored for use in a later attempt.
quiz.explanation: Reflexion uses feedback and remembered lessons; its benefit still needs evaluation.

quiz.question: What changes when a team fine-tunes instead of only updating a memory store?
options: The model’s parameters are updated using training data.
Every future factual answer becomes current.
quiz.explanation: Fine-tuning changes learned behavior, with data quality and evaluation costs distinct from retrieval.
